items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: heard ... Russel "Big Chief" Moore ... at different times when we visited the Metropole

ctx.x: The trip was very agreeable from start to finish. We arrived in New York the 7th of March, and to our surprise, our great friend, George Duvivier, the fine bass man, had reserved a suite of two rooms for us in a hotel called Schuyler on 44th St., between 5th Avenue and Avenue of Americas and told us in a kidding way that he would shoot us if we tried to pay for anything other than food that we would need for breakfast. When we arrived at the hotel there was a big bouquet of flowers for Lily, beer, soft drinks,…

We stayed in New York for 6 days and heard Red Allen, Roy Eldridge, Charlie Shavers, Buster Bailey, Cozy Cole, Claude Hopkins, Coleman Hawkins, Sol Yegar, Russel "Big Chief" Moore and the bassist, Benny Moten at different times when we visited the Metropole on 7th Avenue near Broadway. I didn't find much change in New York from the last time I saw it, but friends told us that there were improvements in the racial relations.

Our first night in the Apple, we had dinner with a Swiss friend, named Peter Wydler and his wife Othella. I was their best man when they married in Paris, France in 1949. Othella, who was American, was a dancer in Catherine Dunham's show which was touring in Europe and Miss Dunham was bridesmaid for Othella and Peter's marriage.
